evidence.note: Upfront decomposition into 6 subsystems (API understanding, package/CLI/build, Vite plugin+next/* interception+RSC, app router/rendering/caching/ISR, pages router, run tests). Order is dependency-aware in the classic sense: resolution/plugin before routing before SSR/SSG. This matches the level-5 anchor: major subsystems identified with a sensible order.

Re-decomposed the Pages Router into finer tasks (router singleton, server pipeline, hydration entry, virtual modules) as build coupling emerged — evidence of revisiting the plan, nudging above a flat static list.

Verification was a single lumped 'run tests until all pass' task rather than per-milestone done-criteria; the first full test run occurs only after essentially all subsystems were already written — a big-bang integration, NOT the early testable vertical slice the level-8 anchor requires.

The long tail is dominated by fighting npm offline-cache install mechanics, not milestone advancement — no through-line of test-gated subsystem completion, so it falls short of the level-8/10 'each milestone tied to concrete tests that prove it' pattern.

reasoning: The agent clearly identified the major subsystems and sequenced them in a sensible dependency-aware order (understand→plugin/resolution→app router→pages router→tests) and maintained/re-decomposed that task list as coupling emerged, which is squarely the level-5 anchor with a slight lean toward re-planning. However, it deferred all verification to a single end-of-build test run instead of establishing a minimal end-to-end route-under-dev slice and gating each milestone on concrete fixtures/tests, so it does not reach the level-8 'testable vertical slice before layering' bar. I place it at 5 (with a modest re-decomposition credit but no early test-gating).
